standard_prerequisites.name: Classical topological Ramsey-space fusion and Ramsey properties
standard_prerequisites.statement: Use the metric-closed topological Ramsey-space setting stipulated in source470. Basic cones[a,A] are Borel, each finite downset{s:s<=fin r_n(A)} is finite, fusion sequences have the stated limit, and the two fusion conclusions474-480 and finite Borel-color homogenization484-486 hold.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Todorcevic, Introduction to Ramsey Spaces; exact properties supplied in source449-486.
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides individual homogeneous refinements and fusion limits, not the separated-cover scheduling or its hyperfinite finite-component construction.

standard_prerequisites.name: Classical countable Borel equivalence-relation facts
standard_prerequisites.statement: A CBER is the union of countably many graphs of Borel involutions. Hyperfiniteness is equivalent to being an increasing union of finite Borel equivalence relations, and is inherited by restriction to a Borel subset.
standard_prerequisites.use: Convert the constructed finite components into hyperfiniteness and represent an arbitrary E by bounded-degree graphs.

standard_prerequisites.name: Finite Borel vertex coloring for bounded-degree irreflexive graphs
standard_prerequisites.statement: Such a graph has a finite Borel proper vertex coloring (Kechris-Solecki-Todorcevic).
standard_prerequisites.use: Applied to a bounded graph-distance power before the Ramsey homogeneous refinement.

core_obligations: Construct the separated-marker edge filtration, prove each component contains at most one new marker and keep the diameter bound 2(f(n)+1), giving finite components.
Schedule all finite approximation cones in a fusion construction so each point of the final cone belongs to infinitely many separated B_n.
Represent the arbitrary CBER by increasing bounded-degree involution graphs and apply the proved separated limsup criterion to the final cone.

proof_roadmap.step: Add edges only through current separated markers; two markers in one component would violate separation, giving the2(f(n)+1) diameter recurrence.
Properly color the graph-distance power and apply the declared classical Ramsey property.
Enumerate the finite approximation downset at each fusion stage and refine successively, assigning each cone a fresh graph index.
Use the Borel-involution decomposition and the full separated-cover theorem to finish the positive-cone claim.

difficulty_reason: The marker filtration and the finite-cone fusion schedule are nonroutine construction obligations even with the stated classical Ramsey fusion and Borel-coloring inputs.

The new theorem covers an arbitrary CBER on an arbitrary metric-closed topological Ramsey space, using a different separated-cover argument.
The source states these earlier works establish the Ellentuck-space case, not the full arbitrary-Ramsey-space claim. Final semantic comparison still required.

editorial_notes: The author explicitly assumes metric closedness for the Ramsey space at470, so the counted statement is read with that source-global convention. Only the listed classical Ramsey-space properties are free inputs; the separated-cover criterion and fusion scheduling are proved.

In641 the indices of theB-set interval are shifted by one stage. The construction638-639 assigns the cones at stage n to k_n<k<=k_(n+1). A point C in[A] is below A_(n+1), so its relevant prefix cone lies in the B_k selected at that same stage. The original641 is preserved and this bookkeeping interpretation requires independent confirmation.

In the diameter argument602-605, a component with no current marker is unchanged. A component with one marker consists of its old component together with the old components joined by the new edges of G_(n+1) restricted to B; all paths then have length at most2(f(n)+1). The displayed union604 is read within that restricted vertex set.
The later generic-comeager theorem664-676 is not used or counted here; no inference about saturation of a meager set is needed for this task.

For a point in the limit cone, the source fusion property supplies infinitely many stages/prefixes. The same-stage indices638-639, together with membership below every laterA, give infinitely many distinct B_k memberships.
